claim: A repair this round created a new conflict at an edge. The VEL0-01 fix (§7.7's precedence, l.11379-11382) lets a dossier population fall empty a locked or pinned dwelling by a `relet` down: 'even a protected dwelling's last household, its building then standing empty but never `vacate`d, so it keeps its state, shell, existence and every locked path'. §2.6's one statement of the clamp (l.2110-2111) says 'a residential building's `households` count lies in [1, capacity]' and that 'the bound holds through every change'; §4.11's `relet` reads that clamp. The edge now has two outcomes. Under §7.7, a building that is not vacant holds 0 households, which §2.6 forbids. Under §2.6, the clamp keeps 1 household, so the dossier's population is not met, against item 8 (f) and §7.7. No text defines how the readers of `Building.households` treat a non-vacant residential building with no household. Those readers are S11's fill, F-PLAN and the plan rung, V06's ledger and departures, and §10.3.
required_change: §2.6's clamp (l.2110-2111) reads: 'a residential building's `households` count lies in [1, capacity] — 0 only for a `vacant` building (§4.11's `vacate`) and for a locked or pinned dwelling a dossier population fall has emptied (§7.7's precedence), which keeps its occupancy state, shell and every locked path and is let again by regrowth's `relet` up like any standing shell — and a non-residential building's is 0'. F-PLAN and the plan rung read that case as a vacant shell's plan (no unit housed), and the generation fill never produces it. §5.3's capacity row gains the lower bound with the same exception.

claim: An `on_enceinte` castle × item 114's wall condition (walls × the castle at their limits; not in the catalogue). The castle's curtain is its own `Enceinte` of kind `bailey` (§2.7 `Castle.curtain`). Along `Castle.cityWeld` the bailey's outer arc and the town wall are 'one wall carrying both enceintes' `wall` roles' (§2.7; §4.8: 'the shared edge is one wall'). Each `Enceinte` carries its own `condition`, `conditionMaterial` and `conditionEpoch` profiles, and every writer works per enceinte: S7's generation row 'writes each run's `Enceinte.condition` and material' for every enceinte it furnishes, the bailey included (§4.8 *Condition at generation*; DR41: 'the enceintes and their stretches'); V06 §3.7.7 decays and repairs each ring on `stream(EVO_FORT, enceinte)` with its own local weight λ; `DeclineOp`'s `breach`/`dismantle` and `wearWall`/`repairWall` name one enceinte. No text says which profile governs the welded stretch. So the one wall is routinely `breached` on the town's profile and `standing` on the castle's, or patched in two materials. §8.2 then draws a whole wall line over a breach, and §11.1 exports the same edge as a wall and as an opening (a battle map's line of sight through a standing curtain). That is a silent contradictory result at TOWN and above wherever the castle sits on the wall and `walls.condition.atGeneration` is on, and at every epoch.
required_change: §2.7, *An enceinte's condition by run*: add 'Along an `on_enceinte` castle's shared stretch (`Castle.cityWeld`) the town enceinte's three profiles are the stretch's one condition, material and epoch: the bailey's profiles there mirror them, written in the same batch by every writer — S7's generation row (one draw for the stretch, on the town enceinte), `DeclineOp`'s `breach` and `dismantle`, `wearWall`, `repairWall` and V06 §3.7.7's transitions, whichever of the two enceintes the op names — and never written apart.' §4.8 *Condition at generation* and V06 §3.7.7 (2)–(3) cite it (V06: the stretch decays and is repaired on the town ring's draws and λ). Add to §13.2's item-114 group a CITY fixture with an `on_enceinte` castle at a vulnerable, poor town's generation shares and over 10 epochs: the welded stretch's two profiles equal at every commit; §8.2 draws one state; §11.1's VTT gives one wall-or-opening answer per edge.

claim: A raised way crossing a city wall × the round-1 support step (VEW-11 × VEW-12, both repairs). §2.7's support step (3) now makes 'an enceinte's wall strip (`Enceinte.strips`)' an obstacle that no pier may stand in. It also adds the clear-span bound: a merged clear span longer than `raisedWays.structure.maxClearSpanM` (masonry 30 m, timber 20 m; V11 §3.24.2) drops a generated course (`raised_too_long`) and bends a declared one. The only crossings of a wall allowed are 'on a gate's line or as the aqueduct's wall arch' (§4.3 *Where it may not go*; §4.13's wall row: '… no support in a wall strip'). The strips are band 2–3 m + inner setback 6–10 m + outer setback and glacis 10–20 m: 18–33 m (§4.8). With a moat it is band + inner setback + berm + the channel (c14 `era.moatWidthM` 8–16 m, c15 10–18 m), and the intervallum lane or a gate plaza is a further obstacle. So the span over a wall runs about 18–42 m. Every timber viaduct, and a large share of masonry aqueducts and viaducts, that must cross the wall is dropped. Two things then contradict it: §4.3, which carries a generated aqueduct 'crossing the wall through an arch', and V06 §3.7's raised gate, 'a gate whose tower carries the deck' — 'the deck's support' standing in the strip.
required_change: §2.7's support step (3): add 'Where the course crosses an enceinte's trace — on a gate's line or as the aqueduct's wall arch (§4.3) — one station stands on the trace: the raised gate's tower (a viaduct or elevated road; V06 §3.7) or the curtain under the aqueduct's arch carries the deck there, its pier the wall's band (no footprint of its own); the strip's setback and glacis parts, the berm and the moat stay clear, and the clear-span bound reads the spans on either side of that station.' §4.13's wall cell reads 'no support in a wall strip but the crossing's station on the band'. V06 §3.7's 'a wall opening under an aqueduct is no support' is amended to match: the opening carries the span, and its stretch is taken as a raised gate's stretch is, after the aqueduct goes. T110-2 gains: a CITY masonry aqueduct across a moated c15 wall with an intervallum, and a timber viaduct on a gate's line — both built, 0 piers in a setback, glacis, berm or moat, every clear span ≤ its bound.
